stemMd: Which mixture is most suitable for making an acid–base buffer?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Equal volumes of two inert gases

options.label: C
options.textMd: A weak acid and a substantial amount of its conjugate base

options.label: D
options.textMd: Only a strong acid with no conjugate-base reservoir

options.label: E
options.textMd: Only sodium chloride dissolved in water

explanationMd: A weak acid can consume added base and its conjugate base can consume added acid. Having substantial quantities of both resists pH changes over a limited addition range.

distractorRationale.e: The salt of a strong acid and base does not provide this buffer pair.
distractorRationale.a: Water alone has little buffer capacity.
distractorRationale.d: This lacks the weak-acid/base buffering pair.
distractorRationale.b: They do not provide the relevant acid–base pair.
